scenes.title: Companion Capture
scenes.caption: Your desktop, remembered by your own Memory.
scenes.narration: Companion Capture lives in your menu bar and saves what you see and edit on this computer to your own Companion Memory.

scenes.caption: Setup says what it records before it records anything.
scenes.narration: The first-run assistant starts by saying what it records. Then it connects to your Core and asks for permission. Nothing is captured until you have signed in or added a key.

items.alt: Welcome to Companion Capture: step one of four, What it does. Three lanes, Screens, Activity and Files, flow from this computer to Your Memory.

scenes.title: Three lanes
scenes.caption: Each lane says what it takes, in its own words.
scenes.narration: Screens takes a picture now and then and skips near-identical frames. Activity notes which app and window you are in. Files watches documents you edit, in folders you choose.

items.label: Activity
items.value: which app and window you are in

items.label: Files
items.value: off until you pick a folder

scenes.caption: Point it at your Core. Sign in from the menu bar.
scenes.narration: In Settings you give it your Core's address, on your network or your Tailscale network, and sign in with your browser or an API key.

items.alt: Settings, Connection: your Core's address, authentication by API key or OIDC browser login, and this device.

scenes.title: What it will not read
scenes.caption: A sensitive-file list you cannot switch off.
scenes.narration: SSH keys, keychains, AWS credentials, GPG keys and password vaults are on a list you cannot switch off, checked before any file is fingerprinted. Crash reports hold panics only, and one setting turns them off.

items.label: Never read
items.value: ssh keys, keychains, AWS credentials, password vaults

items.label: Files lane
items.value: off until you add a folder

items.label: Crash reports
items.value: panics only, one setting to turn off

scenes.title: Installers for the three desktops
scenes.caption: Some lanes are macOS first. The README lists which.
scenes.narration: There are installers for macOS, Windows and Linux. A few lanes are macOS first, and the README says which.
